questions.prompt: Verify that \((2,-1,1)\times(1,3,0)\) is orthogonal to both input vectors.
questions.answer:

Final answer: The cross product is \((-3,1,7)\), orthogonal to both vectors.

questions.prompt: Prove that \(\mathbf a\times\mathbf a=\mathbf0\) using index notation.
questions.answer:
We need to evaluate or prove the stated Levi-Civita/vector expression.
Method: Use permutation parity, determinant products, or epsilon-delta contractions as appropriate.
\[(\mathbf a\times\mathbf a)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}a_ja_k.\]
Interchanging dummy indices \(j,k\) gives
\[\epsilon_{ikj}a_ka_j=-\epsilon_{ijk}a_ja_k.\]
The expression equals its negative and must vanish.
Final answer: \(\mathbf a\times\mathbf a=\mathbf0\).

questions.prompt: Prove the Jacobi identity \(\mathbf a\times(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c)+\mathbf b\times(\mathbf c\times\mathbf a)+\mathbf c\times(\mathbf a\times\mathbf b)=\mathbf0\).
questions.answer:
We need to evaluate or prove the stated Levi-Civita/vector expression.
Method: Use permutation parity, determinant products, or epsilon-delta contractions as appropriate.
Apply BAC-CAB to each term:
\[\mathbf b(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c)-\mathbf c(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b)+\mathbf c(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf a)-\mathbf a(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c)+\mathbf a(\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf b)-\mathbf b(\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf a).\]
Symmetry of the dot product cancels the terms pairwise.
Final answer: The cyclic sum equals \(\mathbf0\).
